proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a successful published derivation satisfying the two hypotheses. By \(\textnormal{lem:published-trace-scheduling}\), the input-determined machine simulates its recursive tasks in dependency-topological order. In particular, after every scheduled step its labelled normalized kernels equal the corresponding published kernels after gate reinsertion, its remaining worklist is the unexecuted suffix, and it has registered exactly the same context masses and fixing margins. The simulation lemma also shows that this successful path cannot be sent to a residual failure state.

For completeness, the initial equality used by the simulation is
\[
 q_s(v)=\frac{p_H(v,s)}{p_H(S=s)},
 \qquad
 p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v,s)>0,
\tag{7}
\]
for every published context \(s\in H\). At a prescribed fixing step the two constructions use the same margin
\[
 m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D},
\tag{8}
\]
and the equality of predecessor and successor descriptions is the exact cross-multiplied identity \(m_{s,W}(K_{s,D}/m_{s,W})=K_{s,D}\). At an ancestor marginalization or a district split, finite distributivity gives the same ordered sum--product circuit. These are the algebraic equalities, not additional identifying assumptions.

Let \(F_H=P/D\) be the accumulated reduced terminal circuit. The proof of \(\textnormal{lem:published-trace-scheduling}\) gives
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=0\pmod{\mathcal J},
\tag{9}
\]
and therefore the residual verifier accepts the compiled projection candidate. Every factor of \(D\) is one of the supported context normalizers, one of the margins in (8), or a reduced factor with the exact ledger decomposition produced by the task invariant. The frozen result \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\) consequently gives
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{10}
\]

The terminal published circuit is identifying by the premise of the theorem. Equation (9), the stepwise circuit equality, and \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) give, for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\),
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}
 =F_H\bigl(O_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}\bigr)
 =T_{a,H}^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}
 =T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{11}
\]
All divisions in (11) are licensed by (10). Every context used in (7)--(11) belongs to \(H\), so the construction neither conditions on nor supplies a law from an absent context. This proves the claim.

added_lemmas.statement: For every well-formed nonterminal state \(\zeta\) produced by the input-determined compiler, exactly one of the following holds: the least actually present selector occurrence yields a selector-correction step; the least unfinished task yields a terminal, nonancestor, district-splitting, or prescribed-complement fixing step; that task satisfies the explicit residual-ready predicate; or the worklist is empty and the completed projection is passed to the residual verifier. Every nonresidual successor preserves the task-kernel and positivity-ledger invariant and strictly decreases \(\mu_H\). In particular, district splitting cannot defeat termination: it replaces one task by finitely many tasks of strictly smaller rank in the well-founded multiset order. No successful nonresidual state is stuck because of an unconstructed margin certificate.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a state reached from initialization. All vertex sets, alphabets, response rows, contexts, and graph predicates are finite by \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\). Hence the gate scan, ancestor sets, postintervention districts, proper ambient districts, and all permutations of a prescribed fixing complement are computable finite sets. Lexicographic minimization is therefore defined whenever the relevant set is nonempty.

We first prove the kernel--ledger invariant by induction over transitions. At initialization, for every \(s\in H\),
\[
 q_s(v)=\frac{p_H(v,s)}{c_s},
 \qquad
 c_s=\sum_{v':(v',s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v',s).
\tag{1}
\]
The index set in \(c_s\) is nonempty because \(p_\theta(S=s)>0\) under exact support, and every summand is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\). Thus \(c_s>0\), and (1) is a positive labelled kernel whose only denominator is in the initial ledger.

A selector correction is evaluation of a known zero--one multiplexer. It changes no denominator, and its equality with the predecessor kernel follows after substituting the stored gate equations. A marginal or ancestor restriction replaces positive cells by finite nonempty sums of such cells. A district split uses the fixed topological quotient of the same kernel. Its conditional factors are ratios of nonempty positive margins, so their numerators are branch-reachable positive margins and their denominators are earlier positive margins. These observations preserve the invariant for every nonfixing successor.

Suppose next that a prescribed fixing prefix has current kernel \(K_j=N_j/D_j\), where every factor of \(D_j\) is already in the ledger and the cells represented by \(N_j/D_j\) are positive on the registered branch. For the next fixable \(W_j\), the finite alphabet \(\mathcal X_{W_j}\) is nonempty, and therefore
\[
 m_j
 =\sum_{x_{W_j}}K_j
 =\frac{\sum_{x_{W_j}}N_j}{D_j}>0.
\tag{2}
\]
Equation (2) is also the required certificate construction: its numerator is the explicit nonempty sum of the current reachable positive kernel cells after multiplication by their common positive denominator, and its denominator consists only of earlier ledger factors. Reducing common factors and normalizing the sign does not change the quotient where \(D_j>0\). With \(K_{j+1}=K_j/m_j\),
\[
 m_jK_{j+1}=K_j,
\tag{3}
\]
so cross-multiplication proves the fixing identity, while (2) proves the new divisor positive. Induction over the finite prescribed complement sequence establishes both the kernel identity and every ledger entry; no certificate is assumed.

We now exhaust the compiler cases. If the gate scan is nonempty, its least member is eligible by the stored selector syntax, giving the first case. If the gate scan and worklist are both empty, the completed accumulated projection is inserted as the first projection candidate, giving the completed residual-verification case. Otherwise select the least task. Empty intervention, a proper ancestor restriction, and a nonempty intervention augmentation are decidable predicates and give their specified operations. If none holds, the district partition is uniquely computable. More than one district gives the split operation. With one district, the recursive case either identifies an ambient district and its prescribed complement, in which case finite enumeration selects the least valid sequence and (2)--(3) make every step eligible, or it is the displayed terminal/failure case. In the latter and only the latter situation the compiler emits a residual-ready token. The alternatives are disjoint because they are tested in fixed order, and they are exhaustive because the last alternative is the conjunction of the preceding predicate failures.

For termination, give a task the lexicographic rank
\[
 r(\tau)=(|R_\tau|,c_\tau),
\tag{4}
\]
where \(c_\tau\) is the finite within-mask phase count consisting of the remaining actual gate occurrences, the remaining prescribed fixing suffix, and the fixed case position. Only finitely many ranks occur for the fixed input. Enumerate them increasingly as \(r_0<\cdots<r_M\), and let
\[
 \mu_H(\zeta)=(n_M(\zeta),n_{M-1}(\zeta),\ldots,n_0(\zeta)),
\tag{5}
\]
where \(n_i\) is the number of unfinished tasks of rank \(r_i\), with the residual-ready marker assigned the least rank. A gate or within-sequence step lowers \(c_\tau\). Ancestor restriction, intervention augmentation, and prescribed fixing strictly reduce \(|R_\tau|\). District splitting removes one task and creates only districts that are strict subsets of its active mask. Terminal completion removes a task. Consequently, at the largest rank whose multiplicity changes, the count falls by one, while only lower-rank counts can rise. Thus (5) decreases lexicographically. This is exactly the finite multiset extension of (4), and lexicographic order on the finite vector \(\mathbb N^{M+1}\) is well founded. This proves progress, invariant preservation, and termination of every nonresidual portion.

added_lemmas.statement: Let Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser have a finite successful derivation that uses only contexts in \(H\) and supported denominators, and order its derivation DAG dependency-topologically with the published stable context and vertex order as tie-breaker. This derivation is used only as a comparison object. After \(k\) steps of the input-determined compiler, the emitted labelled kernels are algebraically equal after gate reinsertion to the first \(k\) published kernels, every registered denominator is the corresponding supported positive margin, and the compiler worklist is the canonically ordered unexecuted suffix of the same recursive tasks. Hence the fixed compiler cannot enter a residual failure state along a successful published recursion, and its accumulated terminal circuit is exactly the published identifying circuit.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix the successful finite published derivation and its stated order, but do not supply it to the machine. We prove the three asserted invariants by induction on \(k\).

At \(k=0\), both constructions initialize every used context \(s\in H\) with
\[
 q_s(v)
 =p_H(V=v\mid S=s)
 =\frac{p_H(v,s)}{\sum_{v'}p_H(v',s)}.
\tag{6}
\]
The denominator is the same supported context mass in both constructions and is positive by (1). The task lists are the same initial recursive query in the same fixed context and vertex order.

Assume the invariant after \(k\) steps. Because corresponding kernels are equal and their graphs and labels coincide, every graphical predicate inspected by the compiler has the same truth value as in the next published recursive case. If an actual forced gate remains, both evaluate the same stored multiplexer occurrence, and gate reinsertion makes the rewritten normalized kernel equal to the published kernel. If no gate remains and the proper-ancestor or intervention-augmentation predicate holds, both compute the same unique vertex set and the same finite marginal. If the postintervention graph has several districts, both compute its unique district partition and create the same proper child tasks in stable order. In the one-district recursive case, both compute the same required district and the same proper ambient district. The compiler fixes only their prescribed complement and uses the common stable order among valid prefixes. Equations (2)--(3) show inductively that its quotient kernel and margin are the same as the corresponding published quotient and supported margin. Finally, an ambient-district terminal case appends the same topological factor and the same marginal.

Thus in every case the next emitted kernel agrees algebraically after gate reinsertion, the newly registered denominator is the same supported margin, and removing the executed task and inserting its canonically ordered children changes both worklists in the same way. This proves the invariant at \(k+1\). It also proves that the compiler's exact cross-multiplied local obligations hold, rather than inferring them merely from semantic equality.

If the fixed compiler reached the residual failure predicate before the published derivation ended successfully, the induction would give the same current task to the published recursion, and all preceding graphical predicates would fail there as well. That is the published failure case, contradicting successful termination. Hence no such diversion occurs. At the final index, all tasks are completed and their ordered sum--product composition is the published circuit. The accumulated circuit is inserted into the projection list, and the preceding algebraic identities give its verifier identity modulo \(\mathcal J\). The successful derivation is therefore simulated by the sole input-determined compiler; it was never installed as an agenda.

proposed_core_edits.name: zeta

proposed.name: zeta
proposed.def: \(\zeta=(\mathscr W,\Gamma,\mathcal J,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathcal L_H^{\mathrm{pos}},\Pi,h,\omega)\), where \(\mathscr W\) is a finite ordered worklist of unfinished tasks \(\tau=(G_\tau,q_\tau,Y_\tau,X_\tau,s_\tau,\mathscr L_\tau)\), \(\Gamma\) is the freshly scanned agenda of actually present selector-gate occurrences, \(\Pi\) is the accumulated labelled projection circuit, and \(\omega\) is the residual or terminal marker. Each task carries its current random and fixed masks through \(G_\tau\) and its ledger \(\mathscr L_\tau\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen scalar-mask state cannot represent the recursively spawned district tasks required by the fixed published case splitter.

proposed_core_edits.name: sigmaTok

proposed.name: sigmaTok
proposed.def: A token \(\sigma=(\tau,s,X,r,x_s)\) records the current task, a supplied context \(s\in H\), an actually present selector-controlled occurrence at \(X\), its primitive gate row \(r\), and the known override \(x_s\). It is created only by scanning the current labelled kernel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Selector tokens must be regenerated from occurrences actually present in the current task rather than preloaded globally.

proposed_core_edits.name: fixTok

proposed.name: fixTok
proposed.def: A token \(\varphi=(\tau,s,W_j,D,D',j,k)\) records the current one-district task, its context, the next vertex in the fixed lexicographically least valid sequence for the prescribed complement \(D'\setminus D\), the required district \(D\), its proper ambient district \(D'\), the prefix index \(j\), and the unique kernel label \(k\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Fixing eligibility must follow the recursive case's prescribed complement rather than an arbitrary currently fixable vertex.

proposed_core_edits.name: elimTok

proposed.name: elimTok
proposed.def: A token \(\ell=(\operatorname{op},\tau,L,Z)\) has \(\operatorname{op}\in\{\operatorname{ancestor},\operatorname{augment},\operatorname{district},\operatorname{terminal}\}\), names the current task \(\tau\), and records the nonempty vertex set or ordered kernel labels computed by that case. District children and terminal factors are stored in canonical input order.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The elimination token must encode the actual recursive task cases, including ancestor restriction, district spawning, and task completion.

proposed_core_edits.name: resTok

proposed.name: resTok
proposed.def: A token \(r=(\tau,K,\mathcal J,\Pi,\mathcal P,\mathcal C)\) stores either the unique graphically residual-ready task or the marker that all tasks are complete, its labelled kernels and constraints, the accumulated projection circuit \(\Pi\), the fixed finite projection list \(\mathcal P\), and the fixed finite list \(\mathcal C\) of tensor products of signed canonical response-row swaps. In the completed case \(\Pi\) is the first projection candidate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Residual readiness must be a graphical failure state independent of verifier success, while completed positive recursions must place their accumulated circuit in the projection list.

proposed_core_edits.name: encH

proposed.name: encH
proposed.def: \(\operatorname{enc}_H(\zeta)\) concatenates, in the fixed topological, context, vertex, district, and response-row orders, every unfinished task graph and mask, every labelled rational kernel, the freshly scanned gate agenda, the constraint and positivity ledgers, the accumulated circuit, the residual candidate lists, and the terminal marker. All component alphabets and lists are finite.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The canonical encoding must include the ordered recursive worklist and per-task ledgers introduced by the repaired compiler.

proposed_core_edits.name: priorityH

proposed.name: priorityH
proposed.def: \(\mathfrak P_H\) recomputes its action solely from the current encoded state. It scans actually present supported-context gate occurrences first; then, for the least task, tests terminal marginalization, nonancestor restriction or intervention augmentation, multiple-district splitting, and the one-district prescribed-complement recursion in that order; only the resulting recursive terminal/failure state is residual-ready. Fixed input orders break ties. No published trace or verifier outcome is an agenda input.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior priority over preloaded tokens is circular and can strand an eligible recursive task behind an ineligible token.

proposed_core_edits.name: muH

proposed.name: muH
proposed.def: Order each unfinished task by \(r(\tau)=(|R_\tau|,c_\tau)\), where \(c_\tau\) is its finite within-mask gate, fixing-suffix, and case-phase count. Enumerate the finitely many input-possible ranks as \(r_0<\cdots<r_{M_H}\) and set \(\mu_H(\zeta)=(n_{M_H},\ldots,n_0)\), where \(n_j\) counts tasks of rank \(r_j\). Reverse rank-count lexicographic order realizes the finite multiset extension: replacing a task by finitely many strictly lower-rank children decreases \(\mu_H\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: District splitting spawns several child tasks, so the old global token counts do not decrease; the finite multiset extension required by the directive does.

proposed_core_edits.name: SACSID
proposed_core_edits.reason: The machine signature is retained, but its implementation must point to the single repaired task compiler rather than an unconstrained token agenda.

proposed.name: input-determined recursive task and agenda compiler
proposed.construction:
An unfinished task is a tuple
\[
 \tau=(G_\tau,q_\tau,Y_\tau,X_\tau,s_\tau,\mathscr L_\tau),
\]
where \(G_\tau\) is the current induced CADMG on the active random mask \(R_\tau\), \(q_\tau\) is its context-labelled rational kernel, \(Y_\tau\subseteq R_\tau\), \(X_\tau\subseteq R_\tau\setminus Y_\tau\), \(s_\tau\in H\) is its supplied context label, and \(\mathscr L_\tau\) is the inherited positivity ledger. The input-determined compiler initializes
\[
 q_s(v)=\frac{p_H(v,s)}{\sum_{v':(v',s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v',s)}
 \qquad(s\in H)
\]
and scans the stored normalized syntax in the fixed topological, context, vertex, and row order. Its gate agenda contains exactly the selector-gate occurrences actually present in these initialized kernels. It never contains an operation token whose graphical predicate has not yet been evaluated.

After the gate agenda is empty, the compiler selects the least unfinished task in the same fixed input order and applies the following recursion. First it closes an empty-intervention terminal task by the required marginalization. Second it replaces the task by its restriction to the ancestors of \(Y_\tau\) whenever that ancestor set is proper, and it performs the ordinary intervention augmentation by removing from the active mask every vertex that is a nonancestor of \(Y_\tau\) after deleting incoming arrows to \(X_\tau\). Third it computes the districts of the current postintervention graph and, when there is more than one, replaces the parent by the canonically ordered proper-district child tasks. Fourth, in the one-district case, it computes the unique district required by the recursive identification case. If that district lies in a proper ambient district, the compiler fixes exactly the prescribed complement, in the lexicographically least valid fixing sequence contained in that complement, and regenerates the successor task. Each step of this sequence computes its margin from the current labelled kernel by
\[
 K_j=\frac{N_j}{D_j},\qquad
 m_j=\sum_{x_{W_j}}K_j
     =\frac{\sum_{x_{W_j}}N_j}{D_j},
\]
reduces this displayed fraction, and records its numerator as the indicated nonempty sum and its denominator as the already registered positive product. If the district itself is an ambient district, the compiler records the corresponding terminal district factor. It emits a residual token exactly in the recursive terminal/failure case in which the gate scan is empty, neither nonancestor predicate holds, the postintervention graph has one district, and no proper ambient district supplies the prescribed fixing recursion. Thus residual readiness is the conjunction of failures of explicit finite graphical predicates, independently of whether any residual verifier candidate passes.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires a single explicit compiler determined solely by the normalized input and current task state.

proposed.name: current-task selector-correction transition
proposed.construction: For the current least task, write \(\zeta\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}}\zeta'\) when the compiler's scan finds a least selector-gate occurrence \(\sigma=(s,X,r,x_s)\) actually present in its labelled context kernel. Necessarily \(s\in H\), and the stored zero--one multiplexer has intervention status one and value \(x_s\) at that occurrence. Replace only that occurrence by \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\), substitute \(x_s\) in its children, append the resulting coordinate-copy equalities to \(\mathcal J\), and rescan the successor kernel. Initialization uses the displayed context normalizer \(p_H(S=s)=\sum_v p_H(v,s)\); the gate rewrite introduces no division. The transition is eligible precisely when its finite syntax check and its cross-multiplied polynomial identity modulo \(\mathcal J\) hold.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Selector correction must consume only a currently present occurrence produced by the deterministic scan.

proposed.name: prescribed-complement reachable-fixing transition
proposed.construction:
For the least one-district task selected by the compiler, let \(D\) be the district required by the recursive case and let \(D'\) be its computed proper ambient district. Write \(\zeta\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\zeta'\) only for the next vertex \(W_j\) in the compiler's lexicographically least valid fixing sequence of the prescribed complement \(D'\setminus D\). Thus no vertex of \(D\) and no arbitrary vertex of \(Y_\tau\) is eligible. At prefix \(j\), eligibility requires
\[
 \operatorname{dis}_{G_j}(W_j)\cap\operatorname{de}_{G_j}(W_j)=\{W_j\}.
\]
Write the current kernel over a common already registered positive denominator as \(K_j=N_j/D_j\), compute
\[
 m_j=\sum_{x_{W_j}}K_j=\frac{\sum_{x_{W_j}}N_j}{D_j},
 \qquad K_{j+1}=\frac{K_j}{m_j},
\]
and register the reduced factors of \(m_j\). The numerator certificate is constructed by the displayed finite summation from the previously reachable positive kernel cells, and the denominator certificate is constructed by concatenating the earlier ledger factors in \(D_j\). Move \(W_j\) from the task's random mask to its fixed mask, check \(m_jK_{j+1}=K_j\) after cross-multiplication modulo \(\mathcal J\), and regenerate only the suffix of this same prescribed complement sequence.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The previous transition allowed an arbitrary fixable vertex; the recursive algorithm requires the prescribed complement and a constructed margin certificate.

proposed.name: recursive task-elimination and district-splitting transition
proposed.construction: Write \(\zeta\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\zeta'\) for the operation produced by the compiler in one of its nonfixing recursive cases. An ancestor operation replaces \((G_\tau,q_\tau,Y_\tau,X_\tau)\) by the induced ancestor task and the exact marginal kernel \(\sum_{R_\tau\setminus\operatorname{an}(Y_\tau)}q_\tau\). An intervention-augmentation operation removes the computed nonempty nonancestor set from the active random mask. A district operation computes all districts of the current postintervention graph and replaces one parent task by the canonically ordered child tasks, each on a strict subset of the parent's active mask. A terminal operation removes the completed task and appends its required marginal or ambient-district factor to the accumulated projection circuit. Every operation is admitted only after expanding and checking its finite polynomial identity modulo \(\mathcal J\). After cancelling common factors and normalizing signs, every new denominator is registered only in its explicitly computed form as a positive rational constant times earlier ledger entries and nonempty sums of branch-reachable positive kernel cells.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The recursion must manipulate explicit tasks and account for child tasks created by district splitting.

proposed.name: compiled terminal-or-residual verification transition
proposed.construction:
Write \(\zeta\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\zeta'\) only after the compiler has either completed every task or produced the unique residual-ready task characterized by failure of the graphical predicates in the initial-token compiler. In the completed case, the accumulated rational circuit is inserted as the first projection candidate. In the failure case, the residual token stores the irreducible task, its exact kernels and constraints, the fixed finite projection library, and the fixed finite signed-row-swap library. A projection \(P/D\) passes exactly when every reduced factor of \(D\) has the constructed positivity-ledger factorization and
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=0\pmod{\mathcal J}.
\]
A contrast passes exactly when its two rational-affine primitive-coordinate maps lie in \(\mathcal I_H\) throughout their recorded rational box, have identical substitutions into \(o_H^N\), have a target difference of certified constant nonzero sign after substitution into \(t_{a,H}^N\), and satisfy all primitive-probability, admissible-cell, and exact-support sign tests. The transition emits the first passing candidate in encoded order, consumes the residual token, and halts. Candidate acceptance is not part of the definition of residual readiness.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Residual readiness must be independent of candidate acceptance, and a completed successful recursion must expose its compiled projection to the verifier.

proposed.name: support-aware recursive completeness handle
proposed.construction: The support-aware handle consists of the retained normalized carrier, the sole input-determined task compiler, and exactly the four transition relations \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\), and \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\). The compiler recomputes its agenda from the current graph and labelled kernels: it scans actually present supported-context gates, then applies the fixed recursive order of terminal marginalization, nonancestor restriction or intervention augmentation, district splitting, and the prescribed-complement fixing recursion, and otherwise emits the explicit residual state. Polynomial constraints and the positivity ledger travel with every task. Neither a successful external derivation nor a verifier-accepted residual candidate is an input to agenda construction.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The high-level handle must expose the sole input-determined task compiler and its independently defined residual state.

proposed.name: executable input-determined SA-CS-ID task machine
proposed.construction: Initialize the context kernels and worklist by the input-determined compiler and encode the resulting state by \(\operatorname{enc}_H\). At each nonterminal state, recompute the least applicable case from the current tasks under \(\mathfrak P_H\) and apply only its corresponding relation among \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\), and \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\). A nonresidual successor is admitted only after its finite graphical test, exact polynomial identity, and explicitly constructed ledger factorization have succeeded. The residual relation is scheduled exactly at the independently characterized recursive terminal/failure state; it halts only when its verifier accepts a projection or contrast candidate. The task-rank count vector \(\mu_H\), which realizes the finite multiset extension of the per-task order, is required to decrease at every nonresidual successor.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The executable machine must regenerate tasks by the published recursive case splitter and use the task-multiset descent.

proposed.statement: Whenever Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser return an identifying functional using only selector values in \(H\) and denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})\), \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\) such that \(O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H\) and \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\). Gate reinsertion makes the returned circuit and its required positive margins algebraically equal to the published derivation on the original expansion.
proposed.justification: Completeness is useful only if it retains the positive formulas already justified by the anchor algorithm.
proposed.gap: The fixed-support normalization requires a proof that one deterministic task compiler simulates, rather than imports, every successful support-licensed published recursion.
proposed.consumer: Existing systematic-selection analyses obtain the same estimand and can adopt the normalized backend without changing valid reported formulas.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The preservation proof now consumes the input-determined progress and trace-simulation lemmas required by the directive.

proposed.statement: Each eligible selector-correction, reachable-fixing, labelled-elimination, and residual-compilation transition preserves the represented observation-target relation on its registered branch domain after composing its emitted circuit, and discharges exactly its displayed polynomial identity or inequality obligation. For every nonhalting transition \(\zeta\Rightarrow\zeta'\), \(\mu_H(\zeta')<_{\mathrm{lex}}\mu_H(\zeta)\): selector correction removes one \(\sigma\)-token, fixing removes one active vertex, elimination removes a nonempty active set or one \(\ell\)-token, and residual compilation removes the sole residual token and enters a terminal state. Therefore the deterministic schedule terminates after finitely many encoded transitions, conditional only on the residual verifier finding a candidate.
proposed.justification: The calculus is executable only when every scheduled task move has a decidable eligibility test, an exact successor, and a well-founded worklist decrease.
proposed.gap: A global token count does not account for district splitting; the repaired basis uses the finite multiset extension of recursive task ranks.
proposed.consumer: A selector-aware implementation can reject malformed task transitions and replay every certificate from its encoded state log.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The already-established local transition argument must be rebased on the repaired recursive task state and the multiset progress lemma before downstream completeness can consume it.

proposed.statement: For every input \((G^{+},H,A,a,Y)\) satisfying the model assumptions, the machine whose schedule contains only \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\) terminates and returns exactly one sound certificate. On each transition the stated local polynomial obligation holds and \(\mu_H\) decreases lexicographically. It returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\), with \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\), if and only if \(T_{a,H}(\theta_1)=T_{a,H}(\theta_2)\) for all \(\theta_1,\theta_2\in\Theta_H\) satisfying \(O_H(\theta_1)=O_H(\theta_2)\); otherwise it returns a support-exact global-twin box. Thus \(F_H\) is partial on the ambient simplex but covers the complete compatible fixed-support image on an identified branch. This strictly completes Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser for the declared fixed-support class without adding a selector context.
proposed.justification: The theorem would turn the repaired sound recursion into a complete fixed-support causal identification calculus once residual exhaustion is proved.
proposed.gap: The nonresidual compiler is now constructive, but the general interacting-district rational-projection-or-global-contrast alternative remains the exact unresolved step.
proposed.consumer: After residual exhaustion is proved, CRAN dosearch could expose a selector-provenance backend whose positive and negative outputs have complete model-level semantics.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline must consume the repaired compiler and progress layer while retaining the sibling-owned all-residual dichotomy as its unresolved residual premise.

proposed.statement: If \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), every selector gate is laid back on \(E_H\), and \(S\) has no latent root shared with \(V\), then \(G_H^N\) is the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\), \(\Phi_H\) equals its ordinary observational-target relation, and \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) reduces to the ID formula-or-hedge classification of Shpitser and Pearl.
proposed.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that the new calculus agrees with classical completeness when systematic selection disappears.
proposed.gap: The normalized graph and nonresidual recursion collapse to ordinary ID, but exact encoding of every finite-categorical hedge twin in the frozen residual candidate format is not yet proved.
proposed.consumer: Implementers can use the proved structural and nonresidual collapse now, and can regression-test complete outputs once the ordinary residual compiler is certified.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The structural reduction now consumes the repaired task compiler, but its formula-or-hedge residual compiler remains an explicit open proof obligation.

proposed.comparator_claim: Algorithms 1--2 are sound, specified failure branches imply nonidentification, and completeness is conjectured.
Ordinary semi-Markovian ID is complete through identifying formulas or hedge countermodels.
Positive gID is sound and complete by reduction to classical ID subproblems.
Root-control CSI identification is equivalent to finitely many ordinary graphical identification problems.
Finite canonical SCMs represent all categorical counterfactual distributions and yield sharp polynomial-program bounds.
The arithmetic-circuit method is at least as complete as classical ID and do-calculus under strict positivity and can exploit additional model constraints.
Sufficient pruning and transit-clustering conditions preserve identification conclusions and transport do-calculus functionals.
Influence-function and weight-based estimators are derived for broad classes of identified effects in hidden-variable graphical models.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparator table must not say that the Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser conjecture or the ordinary formula-or-hedge endpoint is already matched while both residual compilers remain open.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The sibling-owned all-residual dichotomy must prove that every graphically residual-ready task has a verifier-accepted rational projection or support-exact global contrast.
open_obligations.obstruction: Neither the frozen candidate-list definition nor the repaired nonresidual compiler excludes an identified residual whose target is fiber-constant but has only a nonrational algebraic representative. The available terminal three-observable contrast does not lift through arbitrary interacting districts and observed descendants.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser district and fixing recursion was compiled through every nonresidual case, and the negative route was compared with canonical response-row perturbations plus rational interior mixing. The unresolved step is simultaneous preservation of every supported context after lifting a common contrast, or a proof that the projection library contains a rational circuit in every remaining identified case.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The nonresidual compiler now has an input-determined progress and termination proof, and successful supported Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser derivations are simulated exactly. Conditional on the still-open assertion that every residual-ready token contains a verifier-accepted projection or contrast, determinism and multiset descent give one terminal certificate. Certificate soundness then yields
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)
 \quad(\theta\in\Theta_H)
\]
on a formula branch, so the target is constant on every fiber of \(O_H\); a returned twin gives two points of one observation fiber with unequal targets. Hence, under residual exhaustion, identification forces the formula branch and nonidentification forces the twin branch. What is not proved is residual exhaustion itself, including exclusion of a fiber-constant target whose observable representative is algebraic but not rational.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The ordinary residual compiler has not been proved to encode every finite-categorical ID terminal formula and every hedge as a verifier-accepted rational-affine canonical twin box.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen signed-row-swap list has no established theorem guaranteeing the exact hedge witness encoding, preservation through arbitrary observed descendants, fixed canonical response tables and independent-root factorization, or the rational coefficient-bound sign certificate required by the verifier.
open_obligations.attempted: The singleton-support normalization and every nonresidual ancestor, district, and prescribed-fixing step were reduced to their ordinary counterparts. A generic appeal to the classical hedge theorem was rejected because it does not by itself construct the required fixed-box candidate record.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Under \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), exact support gives \(p_\theta(S=s_{\emptyset})=1\). Laid-back gates and absence of a root shared by \(S\) and \(V\) imply, by \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), that
\[
 p_\theta(V=v,S=s_{\emptyset})=p_\theta(V=v)
\]
and that the normalized target is the ordinary \(do(A=a)\) target. The repaired nonresidual compiler then applies exactly the ordinary ancestor, district, and prescribed-fixing recursion. The remaining unproved part is the residual compiler: for arbitrary finite categorical alphabets one must encode every successful terminal ID circuit and translate every hedge into rational-affine canonical twins while preserving independent-root factorization, all observed descendants, strict positivity, and the verifier's exact candidate and coefficient-sign format.

prose_updates.tldr: For a finite selector-gated semi-Markovian SCM observed on exactly \(H\), retained support normalization preserves the full observed--target relation. This round repairs the nonresidual SA-CS-ID architecture: a sole input-determined compiler runs explicit recursive tasks, derives each positivity-ledger margin, simulates every successful support-licensed Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser branch, and terminates by a finite multiset/count-vector descent even when district splitting spawns children. General residual exhaustion and the ordinary hedge-to-canonical-twin compiler remain open, so no formula-or-global-twin completeness claim is reported yet.

project_justification.gap: The published systematic-selection recursion is sound and has branchwise nonidentification results, but its completeness is conjectural and its failure construction is not typed as a support-exact, restricted-interior pair preserving every cell of the one supplied joint law. A further implementation-level gap is that a fixed recursion must schedule spawned district tasks without importing a successful derivation as input.
project_justification.niche: Fixed support is neither ordinary observational identification nor gID from separately supplied experiments: absent contexts cannot be invoked, while supported contexts remain coupled by one random selector and shared natural mechanisms.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer constructs the intrinsic normalized carrier, establishes inverse maps to the original fixed-support image, and gives an input-determined recursive task compiler with explicit selector, ancestor, district, prescribed-fixing, ledger, and multiset-progress invariants. It preserves every successful published positive branch. The intended field-level completion still requires the separate all-residual theorem producing either a verified rational projection or support-exact global twins in every irreducible state.

prose_updates.related_work: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024) provide the selector-gated model, Algorithms 1--2, soundness, branchwise nonidentification results, and an explicit completeness conjecture. The present proved positive layer normalizes a declared support while retaining the parameter image and simulates every successful support-licensed recursive branch with one input-determined task compiler; it does not yet settle their completeness conjecture. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022) motivate positivity-aware witness rebuilding for gID, but do not supply the required exact-support common contrast here. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) supply the classical ordinary formula-or-hedge classification; translating an arbitrary finite-categorical hedge into this verifier's rational-affine canonical twin box remains open. Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen (2026) give sufficient pruning and formula transport for general data fusion, not inverse fixed-support parameter maps or all-residual twins. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2021) remain the software consumer reference.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The task compiler and successful-trace simulation remove the nonresidual scheduling circularity, but they do not prove that the finite residual projection and signed-row-swap libraries are exhaustive. A residual may have a fiber-constant target with only a nonrational algebraic representative, or every currently encoded response contrast may alter an observed descendant. The ordinary special case also lacks the required arbitrary-finite-alphabet hedge encoding and rational sign certificate. Boundary-uniform inference, off-domain regularization, and unrestricted quantifier elimination remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established are the inverse fixed-support normalization, local certificate soundness, restricted-support denominator positivity, the new input-determined nonresidual task progress invariant, and preservation of successful published positive formulas. Still to prove are residual projection-or-global-contrast exhaustion, the resulting all-branch completeness theorem, and the exact ordinary hedge-to-canonical-twin residual compiler. The restricted admissible-cell interior imposes no uniform lower bound, and no absent selector context is supplied or inferred. The terminal three-observable classification and paired exact examples remain evidence for, not a proof of, the general residual theorem.

statement_notes.justification: This is now supported by an input-determined simulation theorem rather than by installing the successful published derivation as the machine agenda.
statement_notes.gap: The new proof closes preservation for support-licensed successful branches while keeping residual completeness logically separate.
statement_notes.consumer: Existing systematic-selection formulas can be replayed on the normalized backend with the same supported margins and no added selector context.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the field-level target and is not proved by nonresidual progress alone.
statement_notes.gap: The exact remaining premise is verifier exhaustion at every interacting-district residual, including exclusion of identified nonrational residuals.
statement_notes.consumer: A complete software certificate should not be advertised until that residual premise is proved.

statement_notes.justification: The normalization and nonresidual recursion reduce to ordinary ID, but the full formula-or-hedge output equivalence remains open.
statement_notes.gap: The missing component is an exact arbitrary-finite-alphabet hedge compiler satisfying the frozen rational-box verifier format.
statement_notes.consumer: Implementers may regression-test nonresidual traces now; complete output parity awaits the residual compiler.
